evidence: Row 7 is a source-level product-scope judgment. The smallest conforming app cannot be a static page, single CRUD screen or cosmetic tweak: instruction.md:1 asks for JavaScript/complete-HTML execution with editor, preview, console and shared library; line 3 requires preservation of actual interacted-with successful previews and safe saved-version recovery across two editors. behaviour.md:7-15 requires cancellation, a shared five-second execution budget, live later interactions, actual-preview rollback and source-relative errors; lines 29-40 require revision conflicts, immutable snapshots, restores, retry idempotency and simultaneous-change arbitration. integration.md:9 requires records, history and recognized retry results to survive process restart. environment/Dockerfile:14-23 copies notes/assets and initializes only an empty /app Git workspace; the seed has no snippets or starter implementation. The reward contract has substantive prerequisites: render/judge.toml:25 requires a newly authored marker actually rendered and logged after Run; constraints/judge.toml:25-27 requires a real UI save followed by independent-clean-context server readback, explicitly rejecting a toast, health endpoint or localStorage alone. scoring.toml:1-11 and score.py:40-48 apply both gates and a functional floor before reward. Functional scenarios cover execution lifecycles and history/restore/concurrency, rather than mere control presence. The template scoring policy is retained. All 21 indexed artifact hashes matched; surface-results.json records a scripted authored marker and saved identity 14 retrieved in an independent context with matching fields. That is supporting product evidence only, with the index packaging/source limits retained. No configured-judge reward, mutation score, Oracle result or portal acceptance is asserted; their absence does not change this specific source-level scope judgment.
counterexample: Broken-app challenge: a polished three-pane mock with hardcoded preview/log samples, a successful health endpoint, and Save implemented with localStorage plus a no-op successful POST would fail Render when asked for a new marker and Constraints when the new saved record is loaded in a clean context. Adding actual arbitrary-source execution and shared server writes already requires substantive implementation, and does not satisfy the requested rollback/history/concurrency behavior by itself. Conforming-alternative challenge: a plain-DOM frontend using a different editor widget, control labels and API routes, backed by the prescribed Express/SQLite runtime, can satisfy the task without matching the golden UI. integration.md:3 and policy.md:5 permit frontend/layout/API choices; render/judge.toml:27 matches controls by purpose; constraints/judge.toml:27 accepts server-rendered records without a separate JSON endpoint. Static restored snapshots are explicitly allowed by behaviour.md:13 and app_context.md:18. No row-7 false failure was found for that alternative. These are reasoned source challenges, not executed negative-app judge runs.
